title: T1566 - Phishing
content: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems. Common sub-techniques use malicious attachments, links, or third-party services.

title: T1078 - Valid Accounts
content: Adversaries may obtain and abuse existing accounts to establish persistence, escalate privileges, evade defenses, or access remote resources.

title: T1003 - OS Credential Dumping
content: Adversaries may attempt to extract account login and credential material from operating systems and software.

title: T1055 - Process Injection
content: Adversaries may inject code into processes to evade process-based defenses or execute in another process context.

title: T1021 - Remote Services
content: Adversaries may use valid accounts with remote services such as RDP, SMB, SSH, or VNC to move through an environment.

title: T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer
content: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

title: T1027 - Obfuscated Files or Information
content: Adversaries may encode, encrypt, or otherwise obfuscate content to make detection and analysis more difficult.

title: T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact
content: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or networks to interrupt availability, commonly in ransomware operations.

title: T1053.005 - Scheduled Task or Job: Scheduled Task
content: Adversaries may abuse Windows Task Scheduler to execute programs at startup or on a recurring schedule.

title: T1059.001 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
content: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution, discovery, credential access, or defense evasion.

title: T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service
content: Adversaries may exfiltrate data through an existing legitimate external web service to blend with normal traffic.

title: T1070 - Indicator Removal
content: Adversaries may delete or alter artifacts such as files, logs, timestamps, and accounts to reduce evidence of their activity.

title: T1547.001 - Registry Run Keys and Startup Folder
content: Adversaries may add entries to Registry run keys or startup folders so programs execute when a user logs in.

title: T1210 - Exploitation of Remote Services
content: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in remote services to gain unauthorized access to internal systems.

title: T1082 - System Information Discovery
content: Adversaries may collect operating-system, version, hostname, and hardware details from a host.

title: T1087 - Account Discovery
content: Adversaries may enumerate local, domain, cloud, or application accounts to identify targets and privileges.

title: T1018 - Remote System Discovery
content: Adversaries may identify remote hosts and systems connected to the same network.

title: T1071.004 - Application Layer Protocol: DNS
content: Adversaries may communicate using DNS traffic to blend command-and-control activity with expected network protocols.

title: T1041 - Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
content: Adversaries may steal data over an established command-and-control channel.

title: T1074 - Data Staged
content: Adversaries may collect and stage data in a central location before exfiltration.

title: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
content: Adversaries may perform network denial-of-service attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources.
